Modelled after the etymology of English "{{m|en|protein}}": from {{cog|grc|πρῶτος||first}} ― cf. {{zh-l|元|original, first}}, which also acted as the phonetic component of the character.

The choice of this character for the sense of "prion" is primarily due to the nature of prions as proteins, but might also have been influenced by the pronunciation of the word {{m|en|prion}}.

Note that in simplified Chinese and Vietnamese scripts, [[亡]] is written with an upward hook. {{Han etym}}
Originally written {{zh-l|*𦣠}}, an {{Han compound|臣|𡈼|ls=ic|t1=eye|t2=person standing on the ground|nocap=y}} – a person standing up and looking off into the distance. Later {{zh-l|*月|moon}} was added to produce {{zh-l|*朢}}.

The {{zh-l|*臣}} component is now written {{zh-l|*亡}}, making the current form a {{Han compound|亡|月|𡈼|ls=psc|c1=p|c2=s|c3=s|t2=|t3=|nocap=y}}.
